highlights.content: ![](https://www.techtarget.com/rms/onlineimages/machine learning_g1186820873_searchsitetablet_520X173.jpg) Getty Images # Context is king as agents evolve, but problems persist ## Awareness enabled by appropriate data and business logic is one of the differences between agentic applications that properly perform and those that never reach production. ![Eric Avidon](https://cdn.ttgtmedia.com/rms/onlineImages/avidon_eric.jpg) Context makes or breaks an AI agent. It's what gives AI agents the situational awareness to deliver trustworthy, accurate outputs. Without it, all other parts might be in place, but the relevant meaning that powers an agent to perform properly will be absent, dooming it to fail. When provided with proper awareness, agents can [help make medical diagnoses](https://www.techtarget.com/healthtechanalytics/feature/LLMs-struggle-with-clinical-reasoning-study-finds), personalize retail experiences, discover new clients, generate sales campaigns, manage and optimize entire supply chains and monitor vast swaths of data that are impossible for humans to oversee to detect fraud. Sometimes, they're even building other agents. But to deliver those outputs, agents need proper context. They need relevant, high-quality data and task-appropriate [business logic](https://www.techtarget.com/whatis/definition/business-logic), and the ability to discover and ingest them independently. "It's no different than providing context to an employee doing a job," David Menninger, an analyst at ISG Software Research, told TechTarget. "You wouldn't give a junior analyst a task without giving them some context." ![ISG Software Research analyst David Menninger](https://cdn.ttgtmedia.com/rms/onlineimages/menninger_david.jpg) Now, after the laborious task of getting data ready for AI and investing heavily in experimental pilots -- while model reasoning capabilities improved -- some enterprises are ready to put agents into production at scale and reap the benefits. The most advanced organizations already have. But widespread deployment of [multi-agent networks](https://www.techtarget.com/searchapparchitecture/tip/Multi-agent-architectures-How-coordinated-AI-systems-scale) requires difficult work that could take years to complete, according to Menninger. "We'll … gradually eat away at the parts that are difficult, and we'll hopefully, in a several year time period, have tackled the biggest challenges," he said. ## AI success amid failures Despite the time and money that enterprises have invested in agentic AI development, most AI projects don't make it into production. Studies show that the failure rate is going down, which is evidence that enterprises that have addressed the underlying data issues that often stall AI projects are achieving at least some success connecting AI applications with the context they need to deliver trustworthy outputs. But they also reveal that more AI projects still fail than succeed. For example, Deloitte's 2026 [State of AI in the Enterprise report](https://www.deloitte.com/us/en/what-we-do/capabilities/applied-artificial-intelligence/content/state-of-ai-in-the-enterprise.html?id=us:2ps:3gl:aisgm26:awa:CONS:em:K0218784:012626:kwd-430833501819:195648817121:794247818306::&gclsrc=aw.ds&gad_source=1&gad_campaignid=23269751971&gclid=CjwKCAjw6MPRBhBTEiwAd-7Mrwla_c_gzzSu2TNPVBWdBS4INV4yNdYgtukO2OU2-zWBAuwZE-s3mBoCwegQAvD_BwE), released in January, showed only one-quarter of the organizations surveyed have been able to move 40% of their AI experiments -- whether single agents, multi-agent systems, chatbots, traditional machine learning projects or other pilots -- into production. Similarly, Menninger noted that ISG's year-end 2025 research found that about one-third of the 1,200 projects it examined are moving into production, an improvement from 17% a year earlier but still well under 50%. "[Some] enterprises are no longer experimenting with agents," Michael Bendersky, director of research at Databricks, told TechTarget....

Organizations are [moving agents](https://thecuberesearch.com/ai-agents-cannot-scale-without-shared-memory-and-knowledge-infrastructure/) into customer support, software development, sales operations and other production workflows. Yet many of those agents remain stateless, unable to retain durable context, share knowledge with other agents or explain how previous decisions shaped current outputs. That gap is becoming less of a model problem and more of a data architecture problem. In the [latest episode](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1v-Vbqh_UXM) of theCUBE Research’s AppDevANGLE podcast, I spoke with Karthik Ranganathan, co-founder and chief executive officer of Yugabyte, about the company’s launch of Meko, a new data infrastructure platform designed to provide persistent memory, shared knowledge and traceability for multi-agent systems. “Your agentic systems are only as good as the state and the data that you feed them,” Ranganathan said. “The model problems are getting solved really well, and the orchestration problems are getting really good. It’s now the iteration cycles between your data and data infrastructure.” ### Stateless agents are becoming an enterprise bottleneck The first generation of enterprise agents has largely focused on individual productivity. An agent can summarize a document, generate code or automate a repetitive task, often helping a user work faster in the process. That value is real, but it remains linear. The larger opportunity emerges when multiple agents can collaborate across shared workflows, organizational knowledge and business processes. That is where current architectures begin to break down. Agents typically exchange outputs, but not the reasoning, assumptions, context or prior knowledge that produced those outputs. In a human team, that would be equivalent to sharing only final conclusions without explaining how anyone arrived at them. “When you look at teams, there’s really no way for agents to actually share their context, their state, their knowledge, their findings or their reasoning,” Ranganathan said....

highlights.titleZh: Hackers used autonomous AI agent to spy on Thailand's finance ministry
highlights.content: [![Cyber Security News | The Record](https://cms.therecord.media/uploads/The_Record_Centered_9b27d79125.svg)](/) * [Influence Operations](/news/influence-operations) * [Cyber Daily®](https://therecord.media/subscribe) * [Click Here Podcast](/podcast) [✉️ Free Newsletter](/subscribe) ![Thailand](https://cms.therecord.media/uploads/large_Thailand_MOF_06d97d4016.jpg) Image: Chainwit / Wikimedia Commons # Hackers used autonomous AI agent to spy on Thailand's finance ministry Hackers used an autonomous artificial intelligence agent to carry out a cyber-espionage campaign against Thailand's Ministry of Finance, according to researchers who uncovered a hacker-controlled server that exposed the inner workings of the attack. Cybersecurity firm Hunt.io said in a report [released](https://hunt.io/blog/thailand-ministry-finance-targeted-with-hermes-ai-agent) last week that it discovered hundreds of files left publicly accessible on infrastructure operated by the attackers while the intrusion was still in progress. The exposed files included malware, stolen credentials, attack scripts, AI agent logs, and evidence that the attackers had already gained access to multiple systems inside the Ministry of Finance. The researchers have not determined how the attackers initially breached the ministry's network. Much of the operation appeared to have been orchestrated by Hermes, an open-source AI agent released earlier this year by the AI research company Nous Research. The attackers enabled the software's so-called "YOLO mode," allowing it to execute commands without waiting for human approval. Researchers said the agent independently explored the ministry's network, searched internal files, gathered system information and looked for opportunities to gain elevated privileges. The exposed infrastructure also contained exploits targeting several known software vulnerabilities, scripts tailored specifically for the ministry, stolen login credentials, active authentication cookies and a previously undocumented malware family dubbed Hades. The malware appears to function as a custom backdoor designed to maintain persistent access to compromised systems after an initial breach. Hunt.io said it found both Windows and Linux versions capable of remotely executing commands and transferring files. The researchers identified the ministry as the likely target because many of the recovered scripts explicitly referenced the agency's internal infrastructure, including administrative web portals, email systems and document management platforms. Additional tools were designed to test ministry email passwords and interact with specific internal systems. Although Hunt.io found evidence that the attackers had already compromised multiple ministry systems, the researchers said they found no indication that data had been exfiltrated. Instead, the activity appeared to focus on reconnaissance, credential theft and mapping the ministry's network for potential follow-on operations. The firm did not attribute the campaign to a known hacking group but said multiple indicators suggested the operators were Chinese-speaking. Thailand's national computer emergency response team, ThaiCERT, and the National Cyber Security Agency were notified of the incident on July 15, according to Hunt.io. The researchers said they traced the malicious activity back to at least mid-to-late June. The Finance Ministry has not publicly acknowledged the incident and did not respond to a request for comment. Thai cybersecurity officials on Monday [said](https://www.facebook.com/NCSA.Thailand/posts/%E0%B8%81%E0%B8%A1%E0%B8%8A-%E0%B8%A2%E0%B8%81%E0%B8%A3%E0%B8%B0%E0%B8%94%E0%B8%B1%E0%B8%9A%E0%B8%A1%E0%B8%B2%E0%B8%95%E0%B8%A3%E0%B8%81%E0%B8%B2%E0%B8%A3%E0%B8%A3%E0%B8%B1%E0%B8%9A%E0%B8%A1%E0%B8%B7%E0%B8%AD%E0%B8%A0%E0%B8%B1%E0%B8%A2%E0%B9%84%E0%B8%8B%E0%B9%80%E0%B8%9A%E0%B8%AD%E0%B8%A3%E0%B9%8C%E0%B8%88%E0%B8%B2%E0%B8%81-ai-agent-%E0%B8%A1%E0%B8%AD%E0%B8%9A-thaicert-%E0%B8%9A%E0%B8%B9%E0%B8%A3%E0%B8%93%E0...

highlights.content: ![Notebookcheck Logo](fileadmin/templates/nbc_v5/images/logo_alone_header.svg) ![Notebookcheck Logo](fileadmin/templates/nbc_v5/images/logo_simplified_unicolor_t.svg) ![dark mode](/fileadmin/templates/images/moon-filled.svg) ![light mode](/fileadmin/templates/images/sun-filled.svg) ![EN Flag](/fileadmin/templates/images/svg_flags/us.svg) ![DE Flag](/fileadmin/templates/images/svg_flags/de.svg) ![US Flag](/fileadmin/templates/images/svg_flags/us.svg) ![ES Flag](/fileadmin/templates/images/svg_flags/es.svg) ![FR Flag](/fileadmin/templates/images/svg_flags/fr.svg) ![IT Flag](/fileadmin/templates/images/svg_flags/it.svg) ![NL Flag](/fileadmin/templates/images/svg_flags/nl.svg) ![PL Flag](/fileadmin/templates/images/svg_flags/pl.svg) ![PT Flag](/fileadmin/templates/images/svg_flags/pt.svg) ![RU Flag](/fileadmin/templates/images/svg_flags/ru.svg) ![TR Flag](/fileadmin/templates/images/svg_flags/tr.svg) ![SE Flag](/fileadmin/templates/images/svg_flags/se.svg) ![CN Flag](/fileadmin/templates/images/svg_flags/cn.svg) ![HU Flag](/fileadmin/templates/images/svg_flags/hu.svg) # Kimi K3 weights released: China's most powerful agentic AI from Moonshot AI free ![Moonshot AI has released its Kimi K3 AI model weights for free.](fileadmin/_processed_/2/d/csm_Kimi-K3-weights-released-Chinas-most-powerful-agentic-AI-from-Moonshot-AI-free_98da09a9d5.jpg) Moonshot AI has released the weights for its leading-edge [Kimi K3 AI model for free on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/moonshotai/Kimi-K3). The 2.8-trillion-parameter AI model comes with a 1-trillion-token context window, enabling the AI agent to process long documents and tackle complex tasks with ease. Business developers, researchers, and AI enthusiasts with very high-end compute systems can now run Kimi K3 locally at no additional cost. Kimi K3 launched in July 2026 and immediately [ranked among the top five most powerful agentic AI](https://arena.ai/leaderboard/agent) on the planet, according to the Arena Intelligence (formerly LMArena) leaderboard. It is currently ranked third on the Agent Arena, and eleventh on the Text Arena. Although Claude Fable and other proprietary AI models top Kimi K3, those AI model weights are not available for download for free use. Business users and AI researchers who are interested in using the free AI model should know that system requirements will be quite heavy to support the non-distilled 1+ TB model, such as an [Nvidia DGX B200](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/dgx-b200/) with 1,440 GB of total GPU memory to load the full model and an [AMD EPYC](AMD-EPYC-9654-shows-what-96-Zen-4-cores-can-do-by-outbenching-a-Ryzen-Threadripper-PRO-5995WX-by-almost-30-on-PassMark.683335.0.html) system with terabytes of RAM and storage. System requirements will drop significantly once Kimi K3 has been distilled, hopefully allowing it to run on properly configured consumer PCs like the recent [Bosgame VTA‑439 AI mini PC with 256 GB of RAM](Ryzen-AI-9-HX-470-OCuLink-and-up-to-256GB-RAM-Bosgame-VTA-439-mini-PC-delivers-86-TOPS-for-OpenClaw-and-local-AI-apps.1315092.0.html) ([reviewed by Notebookcheck here](BOSGAME-VTA-439-review-Ryzen-AI-9-HX-470-is-a-great-fit-for-mini-PCs.1321152.0.html) and [sold on Amazon here](https://www.amazon.com/BOSGAME-Mini-5-2GHz-32GB-DDR5/dp/B0H3ZF1Q85?tag=nbcnewsnet-20&tag=nbcnewsnet-20 "Bosgame VTA-439 AI mini PC on Amazon")). Readers who simply want to [chat with Kimi K3 can access it on the web here](https://www.kimi.com/en "Moonshot AI Kimi K3 on the web"). ![Kimi K3 is ranked #3 on Arena Intelligence's Agent Arena leaderboard.](fileadmin/_processed_/6/5/csm_Kimi-K3-weights-released-Chinas-most-powerful-agentic-AI-from-Moonshot-AI-free-b_56fe46385e.jpg) ## Source(s) [Kimi K3 on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/moonshotai/Kimi-K3), [Kimi K3 model license](https://huggingface.co/moonshotai/Kimi-K3/blob/main/LICENSE), [Kimi K3 announcement](https://www.kimi.com/blog/kimi-k3) ![Google Logo](/fileadmin/templates/images/sociallinks/...

Duis aute irure dolor in reprehenderit in voluptate velit esse cillum dolore ![Image](../themes/custom/blog_plus/assets/img/profile.jpg) ### Ad - Header (728\*90 AD) [Data Science](/topics/data-science) [Data Architecture](/topics/data-architecture) # Technological Independence Relies on an Open Source Foundation * By **Sergio Gago, Cloudera** * July 27, 2026 ![Tech independence needs open source](/sites/default/files/inline-images/Tech%20Independence.jpg) In today’s rapidly consolidating tech landscape, a handful of proprietary providers are increasingly dictating the tools, standards, and rules of engagement for how organizations utilize data and AI. Allowing a few concentrated entities to control the underlying architecture of global technology means letting them decide who participates, at what price, and on what terms. This comes as AI investments are accelerating across Asia Pacific, with [IDC](https://my.idc.com/getdoc.jsp?containerId=prAP53348125&)forecasting  AI and generative AI investments in the region to reach USD175 billion by 2028, growing at a compound annual growth rate of 33.6% from 2023 to 2028. As this momentum transitions from experimentation into enterprise systems, the foundation on which AI is built becomes a strategic decision. In the emerging agentic economy, business decision-makers cannot afford to mistake a rented capability for permanent operational control. Many enterprise AI strategies are currently putting the cart before the horse by focusing entirely on the model layer. We treat generative tools as if AI begins and ends with a prompt. It does not. In the rush to deploy these technologies, organizations are focusing entirely on the model layer and overlooking a fundamental truth: AI begins below the model, with data, architecture, and governance. ### Related * ###### [AI Should Meet Data, Wherever It Lives](/story/5034/ai-should-meet-data-wherever-it-lives) * ###### [Putting the Human Back Into AI Saves Lives, Dollars](/story/4614/putting-human-back-ai-saves-lives-dollars) If those foundations are concentrated, opaque, and inaccessible, the AI built on top will reproduce those exact conditions, only faster, and fail at a far greater scale. Open source is the ultimate defense against vendor lock-in and obstacles to innovation. Instead of dependence on a single supplier, organizations can participate in a shared, democratic ecosystem. To build dependable, production-grade enterprise systems rather than impressive demonstrations, leaders must realize that true technological independence relies on three pillars: interoperability, sovereignty, and private AI. ##### 1. Interoperability is freedom of choice Interoperability is essential to a business’s data strategy to prevent permanent vendor lock-in. Interoperability allows an institution to replace one component without changing everything. Or without forcing all of their data into one single place or vendor. An open model running on proprietary data formats, proprietary orchestration, and proprietary cloud interfaces is still a locked system. AI Agents.title: Context is king as agents evolve, but problems persist

AI Agents.content: ![](https://www.techtarget.com/rms/onlineimages/machine learning_g1186820873_searchsitetablet_520X173.jpg) Getty Images # Context is king as agents evolve, but problems persist ## Awareness enabled by appropriate data and business logic is one of the differences between agentic applications that properly perform and those that never reach production. ![Eric Avidon](https://cdn.ttgtmedia.com/rms/onlineImages/avidon_eric.jpg) Context makes or breaks an AI agent. It's what gives AI agents the situational awareness to deliver trustworthy, accurate outputs. Without it, all other parts might be in place, but the relevant meaning that powers an agent to perform properly will be absent, dooming it to fail. When provided with proper awareness, agents can [help make medical diagnoses](https://www.techtarget.com/healthtechanalytics/feature/LLMs-struggle-with-clinical-reasoning-study-finds), personalize retail experiences, discover new clients, generate sales campaigns, manage and optimize entire supply chains and monitor vast swaths of data that are impossible for humans to oversee to detect fraud. Sometimes, they're even building other agents. But to deliver those outputs, agents need proper context. They need relevant, high-quality data and task-appropriate [business logic](https://www.techtarget.com/whatis/definition/business-logic), and the ability to discover and ingest them independently. "It's no different than providing context to an employee doing a job," David Menninger, an analyst at ISG Software Research, told TechTarget. "You wouldn't give a junior analyst a task without giving them some context." ![ISG Software Research analyst David Menninger](https://cdn.ttgtmedia.com/rms/onlineimages/menninger_david.jpg) Now, after the laborious task of getting data ready for AI and investing heavily in experimental pilots -- while model reasoning capabilities improved -- some enterprises are ready to put agents into production at scale and reap the benefits. The most advanced organizations already have. But widespread deployment of [multi-agent networks](https://www.techtarget.com/searchapparchitecture/tip/Multi-agent-architectures-How-coordinated-AI-systems-scale) requires difficult work that could take years to complete, according to Menninger. "We'll … gradually eat away at the parts that are difficult, and we'll hopefully, in a several year time period, have tackled the biggest challenges," he said. ## AI success amid failures Despite the time and money that enterprises have invested in agentic AI development, most AI projects don't make it into production. Studies show that the failure rate is going down, which is evidence that enterprises that have addressed the underlying data issues that often stall AI projects are achieving at least some success connecting AI applications with the context they need to deliver trustworthy outputs. But they also reveal that more AI projects still fail than succeed. For example, Deloitte's 2026 [State of AI in the Enterprise report](https://www.deloitte.com/us/en/what-we-do/capabilities/applied-artificial-intelligence/content/state-of-ai-in-the-enterprise.html?id=us:2ps:3gl:aisgm26:awa:CONS:em:K0218784:012626:kwd-430833501819:195648817121:794247818306::&gclsrc=aw.ds&gad_source=1&gad_campaignid=23269751971&gclid=CjwKCAjw6MPRBhBTEiwAd-7Mrwla_c_gzzSu2TNPVBWdBS4INV4yNdYgtukO2OU2-zWBAuwZE-s3mBoCwegQAvD_BwE), released in January, showed only one-quarter of the organizations surveyed have been able to move 40% of their AI experiments -- whether single agents, multi-agent systems, chatbots, traditional machine learning projects or other pilots -- into production. Similarly, Menninger noted that ISG's year-end 2025 research found that about one-third of the 1,200 projects it examined are moving into production, an improvement from 17% a year earlier but still well under 50%. "[Some] enterprises are no longer experimenting with agents," Michael Bendersky, director of research at Databricks, told TechTarget....

AI Agents.content: [![](https://d15shllkswkct0.cloudfront.net/wp-content/blogs.dir/1/files/2026/02/CUBE-Pod_SAM_banner_1.png) ![](https://d15shllkswkct0.cloudfront.net/wp-content/blogs.dir/1/files/2026/02/CUBE-Pod-2.png)](https://www.thecube.net/events/program/thecube-pod?utm_source=social&utm_medium=medium&utm_campaign=SAbanner) [![](https://d15shllkswkct0.cloudfront.net/wp-content/blogs.dir/1/files/2026/04/SAM_ad_banner_watch_now_on_demand-7.png) ![](https://d15shllkswkct0.cloudfront.net/wp-content/blogs.dir/1/files/2026/04/SAM_ad_square_watch_on_demand-7.png)](https://www.thecube.net/events/ibm/the-transformation-edge?utm_source=social&utm_medium=medium&utm_campaign=SAbanner) [![](https://d15shllkswkct0.cloudfront.net/wp-content/blogs.dir/1/files/2026/06/SAM_ad_banner_watch_now_on_demand-1-3.png) ![](https://d15shllkswkct0.cloudfront.net/wp-content/blogs.dir/1/files/2026/06/SAM_ad_square_watch_on_demand-1-3.png)](https://www.thecube.net/events/hpe/unleash-ai-2025-momentum-series?utm_source=social&utm_medium=medium&utm_campaign=SAbanner) [![](https://d15shllkswkct0.cloudfront.net/wp-content/blogs.dir/1/files/2026/07/SAM_ad_banner_watch_now_on_demand-1-1.png) ![](https://d15shllkswkct0.cloudfront.net/wp-content/blogs.dir/1/files/2026/07/SAM_ad_square_watch_on_demand-1-1.png)](https://www.thecube.net/events/amd/advancing-ai-2026?utm_source=social&utm_medium=medium&utm_campaign=SAbanner) ![](https://d15shllkswkct0.cloudfront.net/wp-content/themes/siliconangle/img/theCube.png) UPDATED 16:10 EDT / JULY 27 2026 ### Yugabyte targets the missing memory and knowledge layer for enterprise AI agents ![](https://d15shllkswkct0.cloudfront.net/wp-content/blogs.dir/1/files/2025/01/Paul-Nashawaty-96x96.png) by [Paul Nashawaty](https://siliconangle.com/author/paulnashawaty/) Enterprise investment in agentic artificial intelligence is accelerating, but the infrastructure supporting those systems is still catching up. Organizations are [moving agents](https://thecuberesearch.com/ai-agents-cannot-scale-without-shared-memory-and-knowledge-infrastructure/) into customer support, software development, sales operations and other production workflows. Yet many of those agents remain stateless, unable to retain durable context, share knowledge with other agents or explain how previous decisions shaped current outputs. That gap is becoming less of a model problem and more of a data architecture problem. In the [latest episode](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1v-Vbqh_UXM) of theCUBE Research’s AppDevANGLE podcast, I spoke with Karthik Ranganathan, co-founder and chief executive officer of Yugabyte, about the company’s launch of Meko, a new data infrastructure platform designed to provide persistent memory, shared knowledge and traceability for multi-agent systems. “Your agentic systems are only as good as the state and the data that you feed them,” Ranganathan said. “The model problems are getting solved really well, and the orchestration problems are getting really good. It’s now the iteration cycles between your data and data infrastructure.” ### Stateless agents are becoming an enterprise bottleneck The first generation of enterprise agents has largely focused on individual productivity. An agent can summarize a document, generate code or automate a repetitive task, often helping a user work faster in the process. That value is real, but it remains linear. The larger opportunity emerges when multiple agents can collaborate across shared workflows, organizational knowledge and business processes. That is where current architectures begin to break down. Agents typically exchange outputs, but not the reasoning, assumptions, context or prior knowledge that produced those outputs. In a human team, that would be equivalent to sharing only final conclusions without explaining how anyone arrived at them. “When you look at teams, there’s really no way for agents to actually share their context, their state, their knowledge, their findings or their reasoning,” Ranganathan said....

AI Agents.content: ![]() ![PR Newswire](https://s3.tradingview.com/news/logo/pr_newswire--theme-light.svg) ![PR Newswire](https://s3.tradingview.com/news/logo/pr_newswire--theme-dark.svg) # Emerson Expands Ovation AI Portfolio with New Intelligent Agents ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/emerson.svg) *New Ovation AI Agents enable operators to resolve complex issues in a fraction of the time for faster, smarter plant operations* PITTSBURGH, July 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Global automation leader Emerson ([![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/emerson.svg)EMR](/symbols/NYSE-EMR/)) today introduced new [Ovation™ AI Agents](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4738228-1&h=3808006670&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.emerson.com%2Fen%2Fautomation-systems%2Fovation%2Fovation-ai%2Fovation-ai-agents&a=Ovation%E2%84%A2+AI+Agents) for the power and water industries, expanding the AI capabilities of the Ovation Automation Platform 4.0 release. AI Agents.content: [![Cyber Security News | The Record](https://cms.therecord.media/uploads/The_Record_Centered_9b27d79125.svg)](/) * [Influence Operations](/news/influence-operations) * [Cyber Daily®](https://therecord.media/subscribe) * [Click Here Podcast](/podcast) [✉️ Free Newsletter](/subscribe) ![Thailand](https://cms.therecord.media/uploads/large_Thailand_MOF_06d97d4016.jpg) Image: Chainwit / Wikimedia Commons # Hackers used autonomous AI agent to spy on Thailand's finance ministry Hackers used an autonomous artificial intelligence agent to carry out a cyber-espionage campaign against Thailand's Ministry of Finance, according to researchers who uncovered a hacker-controlled server that exposed the inner workings of the attack. Cybersecurity firm Hunt.io said in a report [released](https://hunt.io/blog/thailand-ministry-finance-targeted-with-hermes-ai-agent) last week that it discovered hundreds of files left publicly accessible on infrastructure operated by the attackers while the intrusion was still in progress. The exposed files included malware, stolen credentials, attack scripts, AI agent logs, and evidence that the attackers had already gained access to multiple systems inside the Ministry of Finance. The researchers have not determined how the attackers initially breached the ministry's network. Much of the operation appeared to have been orchestrated by Hermes, an open-source AI agent released earlier this year by the AI research company Nous Research. The attackers enabled the software's so-called "YOLO mode," allowing it to execute commands without waiting for human approval. Researchers said the agent independently explored the ministry's network, searched internal files, gathered system information and looked for opportunities to gain elevated privileges. The exposed infrastructure also contained exploits targeting several known software vulnerabilities, scripts tailored specifically for the ministry, stolen login credentials, active authentication cookies and a previously undocumented malware family dubbed Hades. The malware appears to function as a custom backdoor designed to maintain persistent access to compromised systems after an initial breach. Hunt.io said it found both Windows and Linux versions capable of remotely executing commands and transferring files. The researchers identified the ministry as the likely target because many of the recovered scripts explicitly referenced the agency's internal infrastructure, including administrative web portals, email systems and document management platforms. Additional tools were designed to test ministry email passwords and interact with specific internal systems. Although Hunt.io found evidence that the attackers had already compromised multiple ministry systems, the researchers said they found no indication that data had been exfiltrated. Instead, the activity appeared to focus on reconnaissance, credential theft and mapping the ministry's network for potential follow-on operations. The firm did not attribute the campaign to a known hacking group but said multiple indicators suggested the operators were Chinese-speaking. Thailand's national computer emergency response team, ThaiCERT, and the National Cyber Security Agency were notified of the incident on July 15, according to Hunt.io. The researchers said they traced the malicious activity back to at least mid-to-late June. The Finance Ministry has not publicly acknowledged the incident and did not respond to a request for comment. [Become an Insider](/subscription) and start reading now. Have an account? . The tech industry is rallying around open-weight AI, but one major lab is staying conspicuously silent. Anthropic is drawing criticism from across Silicon Valley for not signing an open letter advocating for open-weight AI as Washington considers restrictions on some Chinese models. On Friday, [over two dozen companies](https://www.businessinsider.com/microsoft-nvidia-meta-palantir-jensen-huang-open-source-ai-letter-2026-7) — including Nvidia, Meta, and Microsoft — signed "Open Weights and American AI Leadership," endorsing open-weights, which means developers can download, modify, and deploy AI models on their own infrastructure. Over the weekend, several other major names in AI signed the letter: OpenAI, Google, and SpaceX. LLMs.content: [Asosiy kontentga oʻtish](#main) * [Uzbekistan](/en/uzbekistan/) * [World](/en/world/) * [Society](/en/society/) * [Tech](/en/technology/) * [Sport](/en/sport/) * [Auto](/en/auto/) * [Culture](/en/culture/) * [Economy](/en/economy/) * [Ўзбекча](#) * [O'zbek](#) * [Русский](#) * [Türkçe](#) * [Қазақша](#) * [Français](#) * [Español](#) * [Deutsch](#) # Anthropic Head Comments on Open-Weight Artificial Intelligence Models ·0·[Technology](/en/technology/) Dario Amodei, co-founder and CEO of [Anthropic](/en/tags/anthropic/), one of the leading companies in the field of artificial intelligence, stated that he does not support banning open-weight artificial intelligence models. According to him, the company has never advocated for such restrictions, and rumors to that effect are groundless. This statement comes at a time of heated debate among industry representatives and tech giants regarding the future of open-source technology. This is reported by Techcrunch.com. [reports](https://zamin.uz/index.php?do=go&url=aHR0cHM6Ly90ZWNoY3J1bmNoLmNvbS8yMDI2LzA3LzI3L2FudGhyb3BpY3MtZGFyaW8tYW1vZGVpLXJlc3BvbmRzLWRvZXNudC1vcHBvc2Utb3Blbi13ZWlnaHQtbW9kZWxzLWJ1dC1mZWFycy1jaGluZXNlLWFpLw%3D%3D) . According to ixbt.com, this reaction followed an open letter published on the X social network by [Nvidia](/en/tags/nvidia/) founder and CEO Jensen Huang. In this letter, along with Nvidia, a number of leading companies such as Meta, Microsoft, Mistral, and Hugging Face urged politicians not to rush into placing restrictions on open-weight AI models. Although China was not directly mentioned in that letter, the main debates boil down to claims that Chinese laboratories are expanding their capabilities through intellectual property theft. ## Risks of China in Artificial Intelligence In his blog post, Dario Amodei focused specifically on the issue of security, emphasizing that a distinction must be made between open-weight models and the threats posed by China. He noted that open-weight models lacking dangerous capabilities are beneficial to society and bring great value to researchers and developers. However, his main concern is the attempt by authoritarian governments, particularly the Chinese Communist Party, to create systems even more powerful than those in the U.S. in order to achieve permanent military superiority. The head of Anthropic also expressed concern over the increase in biological attacks and cybersecurity threats. In his view, open-weight models are more dangerous in such scenarios because it is extremely difficult to control their use or impose restrictions on them. Citing a report by the UK Artificial Intelligence Safety Institute, he reminded that once open-weight codes are distributed, they cannot be recalled. ## Experts and Future Measures Open-source advocates argue that access to powerful models, free from centralized control, helps defenders ensure security. However, in contrast, Amodei proposed specific measures to combat China's dominance in AI. He believes it is necessary to restrict China's access to powerful chips and take official measures against distillation processes to prevent intellectual property theft. For reference, the U.S. government has been warning that it may impose sanctions against China if the theft of U.S. company intellectual property is detected. Therefore, the issue of maintaining a balance between freedom of innovation and national security remains at the forefront of today's tech market discussions. LLMs.content: Loading… Suggestions Articles [View all results](#) * [News](https://videocardz.com/sections/news) * [Graphics](https://videocardz.com/topics/graphics) # NVIDIA Reflex 2 remains unreleased 18 months after announcement, RTX owners still waiting Published: Today, 13:53 GMT • WhyCry • [Comments](https://videocardz.com/newz/nvidia-reflex-2-remains-unreleased-18-months-after-announcement-rtx-owners-still-waiting#disqus_thread "Comments") Latest [Send a tip!](https://videocardz.com/send-us-a-tip) [15:53 Jul 27 NVIDIA Reflex 2 remains unreleased 18 months after announcement, RTX owners still waiting](https://videocardz.com/newz/nvidia-reflex-2-remains-unreleased-18-months-after-announcement-rtx-owners-still-waiting "NVIDIA Reflex 2 remains unreleased 18 months after announcement, RTX owners still waiting")[14:38 Jul 27 Gigabyte AORUS RTX 5080 Infinity uses custom PCB with a massive cooler cutout](https://videocardz.com/newz/gigabyte-aorus-rtx-5080-infinity-uses-custom-pcb-with-a-massive-cooler-cutout "Gigabyte AORUS RTX 5080 Infinity uses custom PCB with a massive cooler cutout")[13:33 Jul 27 MSI and Colorful announce RTX 50 price increases for distributors, RTX 5070 Ti now starts 38% over MSRP](https://videocardz.com/newz/msi-and-colorful-announce-rtx-50-price-increases-for-distributors-rtx-5070-ti-now-starts-38-over-msrp "MSI and Colorful announce RTX 50 price increases for distributors, RTX 5070 Ti now starts 38% over MSRP")[12:35 Jul 27 Steam Deck owner builds spiked security system to stop family draining its battery](https://videocardz.com/newz/steam-deck-owner-builds-spiked-security-system-to-stop-family-draining-its-battery "Steam Deck owner builds spiked security system to stop family draining its battery") ## NVIDIA Reflex 2 still without a release date It’s January 2025 and NVIDIA has just announced Reflex 2 at CES 2025. It introduces a new Frame Warp feature designed to reduce input latency by updating rendered frames based on the latest mouse input. The company claimed the technology could lower latency by up to 75% compared with rendering without Reflex. The announcement confirmed support for GeForce RTX 20, RTX 30, RTX 40 and RTX 50 graphics cards. NVIDIA initially named THE FINALS and VALORANT as the first supported games, but neither title has received a publicly available Reflex 2 implementation. Although NVIDIA announced the GeForce RTX 50 series and Reflex 2 around 18 months ago, the technology has still not been released. Despite this, NVIDIA’s official Reflex 2 page advertises the feature alongside a “**Buy GeForce**” button. Had you known Reflex 2 would take this long to arrive, would it have changed your GeForce purchase plans? ### NVIDIA has provided no update on the delay NVIDIA mentioned Reflex 2 several times after the January 2025 announcement. The company referenced it in a February 2025 blog post and its financial materials, while journalists were shown a working demonstration of THE FINALS in March. These mentions repeated the original performance claims but did not include a release date. More than 18 months later, NVIDIA still lists Reflex 2 Frame Warp as “coming soon.” The developer page asks studios to register for notifications about general integration, suggesting that the required SDK has not been released publicly. > It's been more than 80 weeks since NVIDIA announced Reflex 2 in January of 2025. > > Where the hell is it, [@JensenHuang](https://x.com/JensenHuang?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) ?? Modder PureDark reportedly used these components to create [a working Frame Warp demonstration](https://videocardz.com/newz/puredark-releases-free-demo-of-nvidia-reflex-2-frame-warp-works-on-rtx-20-gpus) in October 2025...

Insurance Australia Group (IAG) will "explore" whether customer-facing voice agent technology by OpenAI can help speed up its responsiveness to weather and disaster related claims. The insurer has signed on to use OpenAI's new [Presence](https://openai.com/index/introducing-openai-presence/) agentic AI platform. It intends to look into AI agents handling simple, non-event related claims over the phone, so as to free up human claims specialists to deal with more complex cases faster. "We see an opportunity to use Presence to deploy trusted customer agents that provide timely, reliable support for our customers during moments that matter, particularly during high demand periods such as severe weather events and natural disasters," retail chief executive Julie Batch said in a statement. “Our initial focus will be on where the need is greatest – high volume natural perils – to ensure we help our customers the best way we can at a stressful point in their lives." An IAG spokesperson explained that by using AI agents to help customers lodge simpler, non-event related claims, the insurance giant can reduce call queues and reach others impacted by major events more quickly. OpenAI Presence is not a new AI model, but tooling built around an existing one. Presence combines policies, guardrails, simulations and an evaluation system designed to keep an AI agent within boundaries a company sets for it. Each deployment is scoped to a specific task, such as resolving a billing query or supporting an insurance claim. The agent receives only the knowledge and system access needed for that job, and hands off to a person when a case falls outside its remit. OpenAI has been "dogfooding" Presence for its own English-language phone support, and claimed it resolves 75 percent of inbound issues without human assistance. A Codex-powered improvement cycle cut human handoffs on the support line by 15 percentage points in 10 days, OpenAI said. IAG is looking to implement Presence in the first half of its 2027 financial year, which runs from July to December 2026., the spokesperson said. Presence deployments are led by OpenAI's own forward deployed engineers or selected systems integrators. IAG's engagement with OpenAI has so far centred on solution design, rather than live deployment, the insurer said. The insurer has been exploring the potential of advanced AI voice technologies for some time, the spokesperson told *iTnews*. While the OpenAI partnership is at early stages, IAG sees it as a long-term opportunity, the spokesperson added. **IAG one of three launch customers worldwide** The insurer is one of three launch customers for OpenAI Presence, which was officially announced on July 23 Australian time. AI Product.content: [Asosiy kontentga oʻtish](#main) * [Uzbekistan](/en/uzbekistan/) * [World](/en/world/) * [Society](/en/society/) * [Tech](/en/technology/) * [Sport](/en/sport/) * [Auto](/en/auto/) * [Culture](/en/culture/) * [Economy](/en/economy/) * [Ўзбекча](#) * [O'zbek](#) * [Русский](#) * [Türkçe](#) * [Қазақша](#) * [Français](#) * [Español](#) * [Deutsch](#) # Enigma Raises $70 Million to Simplify Robot Control ·36·[Technology](/en/technology/) A young research laboratory called [Enigma](/en/tags/enigma/), aiming to revolutionize the fields of AI and robotics, has announced its exit from stealth mode and secured $70 million in a seed funding round. According to ixbt.com, this funding round was led by Index Ventures and Ribbit Capital, with its main goal being to make robot control as easy and intuitive as adjusting audio volume. This was reported by Techcrunch.com [reports](https://zamin.uz/index.php?do=go&url=aHR0cHM6Ly90ZWNoY3J1bmNoLmNvbS8yMDI2LzA3LzI3L2VuaWdtYS1yYWlzZXMtNzBtLXRvLW1ha2UtY29udHJvbGxpbmctYS1yb2JvdC1hcy1lYXN5LWFzLWFkanVzdGluZy10aGUtdm9sdW1lLw%3D%3D) . Today, many robotics companies are trying to solve one of the most complex challenges for AI: working on foundational models that enable machines to perform tasks they haven't been trained on before. While some rely on studying millions of web videos or using computer simulations, the sub-one-year-old Enigma has chosen a completely different approach. ## Studying Human-Machine Interaction The startup focuses not on model capabilities, but on how humans interact with robots. The project authors believe that this interaction will lead to intuitive interfaces and an entirely new type of robot brain. To test how humans want to interact with machines, the company is launching a large-scale experiment allowing anyone in the world to interact online with more than 100 of its AI-driven robots. Located in hangars in Israel and California, these robots are capable of painting with a paintbrush, fencing, and performing simple chemical experiments by stirring liquids in flasks. Enigma claims to have developed its robotic arms and the underlying models entirely from scratch. ## Experienced Founders and a Fresh Approach The company was founded by Jonathan, Microsoft's youngest employee in history, and his childhood friend Gal Niv. They conducted cybersecurity research in Israel's elite Unit 8200. Deciding to launch their own startup last year, these guys didn't have direct experience in robotics, but believed that this field contains some of the most exciting challenges in the tech world. Index Ventures partner Shardul Shah noted that unlike many experts in robotics, Jonathan and Gal coming from outside the industry gives them more uniqueness and freedom. Industry insiders often start with control or dexterity capabilities, while Enigma starts from a completely different point — the end-user experience. In an interview with TechCrunch, Jonathan emphasized that Enigma aims to completely simplify communication between humans and robots. AI Product.content: # AI start-up Zelim wins 2026 UK edition of KPMG’s Tech Innovator 27 July 2026 Consultancy.uk 2 min. read ***KPMG’s UK Tech Innovator contest has concluded its annual search the next generation of technological talent. The 13th edition of the event closed with the naming of Edinburgh-based AI start-up Zelim as the nation’s top technology innovator.*** Every year, KPMG’s UK Tech Innovator event looks for the best and brightest tech scale-ups that are lighting up the UK. The competition is open to tech and tech enabled businesses, and applications are now open for the UK competition online. After a hard-fought opening stage, a shortlist of eight regional champions were announced, celebrating innovators across the UK. These included Prospectral in the East of England; Pimloc in London; Supply Chain In-Sites in the North East and Yorkshire; ufuture in the North West; Digostics in South Central; RIG Corp in the South West and Wales; High Temperature Materials Systems in the Midlands; and Zelim in Scotland. The shortlisted entrants were then invited to pitch their business and growth plans to a panel of judges across regional heats – before an overall UK champion was selected. And after that period of deliberation, the firm advancing to the world stage at the KPMG Global Tech Innovator Competition later in the year, is Zelim. The Edinburgh-based start-up builds AI-enabled maritime safety and security systems to save lives when people fall overboard at sea. It will now face an international panel of judges, which will select a global champion. Andy Tipping, from Zelim, said, “We are honoured to be chosen as the winner, especially given the phenomenal crop of tech companies that came to compete from across the UK. 2026 has been a big year for us already, so this award is the icing on top of the cake and is testament to the dedication of the team who worked so hard to bring a genuinely world leading product to market.” The competition has has celebrated some of the UK’s best pure technology and tech-enabled businesses over the years. Zelim joins a hall of fame which includes What3Words, VividQ and HiiROC – all of whom have all been crowned previous winners. Zelim will hope to emulate HiiROC in particular, though, with the 2022 winner eventually going one step further by winning the global final at Web Summit, a tech conference that takes place each year. Nicole Lowe, head of emerging giants at KPMG UK, commented, “Zelim is a perfect example of the UK’s burgeoning tech talent and we wish them the very best of luck as they represent the UK in the Global Final of the competition and look forward to playing a part in the exciting journey they have to come. AI Product.content: APAC # How the AI value chain is reshaping APAC deal flow ## The year’s largest transactions span across LLMs, chips, data centers and energy grids. | By  [Kristie Neo](https://pitchbook.com/news/author/kristie-neo) AI is now behind most of the largest PE and VC deals in Asia-Pacific, from foundational models to the chips, data centers and power grids that support them. Asia’s markets occupy different positions in the AI value chain: China leads frontier model development, South Korea and Taiwan anchor semiconductors, and Southeast Asia is emerging as a digital infrastructure hub. According to PitchBook’s [**H1 2026 APAC Private Capital Breakdown**](https://pitchbook.com/news/reports/h1-2026-apac-private-capital-breakdown), it’s a spread that shows where investor conviction is converging. These businesses are underpinning the next phase of AI adoption, whether in foundational models, semiconductor innovation, cloud infrastructure or enterprise or digital infrastructure. This is driving most large transactions across APAC, underscoring the impact of AI across asset classes. These include [DeepSeek](https://pitchbook.com/profiles/company/606456-91#overview), [ByteDance](https://pitchbook.com/profiles/company/63628-21), [Moonshot AI](https://pitchbook.com/profiles/company/539048-89) and [StepFun](https://pitchbook.com/profiles/company/721081-18) in Greater China; [DayOne](https://pitchbook.com/profiles/company/520873-30#overview) in Southeast Asia; [MegazoneCloud](https://pitchbook.com/profiles/company/266049-82#overview) in South Korea; and [Firmus Technologies](https://pitchbook.com/profiles/company/501786-82) in Australia. On the PE side, the AI story looks different. Rather than frontier models, PE capital is chasing the infrastructure needed to support AI adoption: data centers, cloud capacity, semiconductors, power supply and grid resilience. IT deal value in PE reached $24.6 billion in H1 2026, roughly 90% of the full-year 2025 total, driven by Singapore’s data center platforms, renewable-linked deals in Australia and New Zealand and South Korea’s AI semiconductor ecosystem. That reach isn’t confined to technology. It runs across the value chain into energy, infrastructure and industrial assets too. However, while AI is dominating PE and VC dealmaking, fundraising and exits remain uneven across the region, suggesting it isn’t completely out of the woods yet. Capital concentration is showing up in larger rounds, larger funds and experienced managers, suggesting that investors are re-committing to existing or proven names. But growing IPO pipelines and exit activity in South Korea, Hong Kong and India suggest that liquidity may return to APAC, supporting returns for Asian GPs. Until then, deployment continues to be supported by existing dry powder rather than a wide recovery in new fund formation. Learn more about our [editorial standards](https://pitchbook.com/news/pitchbook-news-editorial-standards-code-conduct).

The 2.8-trillion-parameter AI model comes with a 1-trillion-token context window, enabling the AI agent to process long documents and tackle complex tasks with ease. Business developers, researchers, and AI enthusiasts with very high-end compute systems can now run Kimi K3 locally at no additional cost. Although Claude Fable and other proprietary AI models top Kimi K3, those AI model weights are not available for download for free use. None of them require a license negotiation to download, fine-tune, or run on your own hardware. ### Table of Contents Picking between the three isn’t a matter of brand loyalty. DeepSeek V4 Pro posts a 93.5% score on LiveCodeBench, reportedly among the highest publicly tested model scores as of mid-2026. GLM-5.2 answers back with a 6.7-point lead over DeepSeek on SWE-bench Pro and a 17-point edge on long-horizon agentic coding. Qwen3.6 skips the arms race for the top of the leaderboard entirely, shipping a 27B dense model that runs on a single 18GB consumer GPU under an Apache 2.0 license, avoiding the legal ambiguity that MIT licensing sometimes creates for enterprise procurement teams. Zhipu AI, which runs its API business under the Z.ai brand out of Beijing, followed with GLM-5.2 on June 13, 2026, then extended its context window to 1 million tokens within weeks of launch. That single decision, more than any benchmark score, separates this group from GPT-5.6, Claude Opus 4.8, or Gemini 3.1 Pro, none of which publish downloadable weights. DeepSeek publishes under the [deepseek-ai organization on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai), Zhipu under [zai-org](https://huggingface.co/zai-org), and Alibaba under [the Qwen organization](https://huggingface.co/Qwen). deals](https://www.axios.com/2025/10/23/ai-boom-circular-financing) could create systemic financial risks. * Nvidia shares tumbled 4.5% in late morning trading. **The big picture:** Nvidia, which is making oodles of cash, is using its financial heft to buoy its customers, who are losing oodles of cash. * The company is weighing a plan to guarantee $250 billion for an OpenAI data center project in Investors have also grown increasingly jittery over AI infrastructure spending, calling into question their return on investment.
